artifacts.summary: Audit-surface research: one verified definition-to-theorem conversion (ShiftSet.sep over discrete duration orders), a four-constraint independence programme with three of four witnesses verified, four stale citations corrected, and the inspection-only residue enumerated at 24 Lean definitions (three of them currently unrecorded).

memory_candidates.content: A file:line citation that crosses a repository boundary is outside every gate: check C20's declaration-span cross-check only reads this repository's live scope, so a table maintained in a consuming repository rots silently. Four citations drifted by a uniform +38 and landed inside a different theorem while every in-repo citation stayed green. The fix is the one paper-definitions-of-record.md already applies to the paper side: cite declaration names, generate any line-numbered export.

Narrowing a transcription audit has two distinct surfaces that are easy to conflate: the definitional surface (Lean definitions a human reads against paper text) shrinks only when a paper notion stops being transcribed because Lean derives it; the construction's axiom burden (facts a particular certified object supplies by hand) shrinks whenever a supplied field becomes a derived theorem. Converting a structure field to a theorem moves the second number, not the first.

omega is blind to goals typed at TemporalOrder carriers: a hypothesis at intOrder.carrier is not syntactically Int, so omega reports 'no usable constraints'. State the arithmetic over Int and cross into the carrier with show, or replace omega with explicit lt_irrefl/le_trans steps. The same coercion opacity defeats instance synthesis for SuccOrder over a TemporalOrder carrier, which is why Std.lean uses the explicit @ plus inferInstanceAs form.
